evidence: Killed a real child worker with SIGKILL (returncode -9 confirmed in every case) at seven precise points and inspected the durable state left behind: before os.link inside write_once with a 2 MiB payload, after os.link but before the directory fsync, before os.replace inside replace_atomic, between two hash-chained events, after staging bytes but before any commit, after the durable commit but before the callback, plus an in-process rewrite attempt against an immutable file. Ran python3 -I commit_boundary_injector.py (exit 0, 7 fault classes, all PASS) and python3 -I -m unittest discover (12 tests, OK). Observed: no half-written immutable file ever became visible; the linked-but-unfsynced event was byte-exact and self-consistent; generation 1 of recovery-state.json survived the mid-replacement crash intact; verify_chain returned zero errors after every crash; the pre-commit case was refused at ingestion with RECOVERY_REQUIRED and a read-back failure; the post-commit case left 1796 readable bytes plus an intact immutable capsule; write_once raised FileExistsError on differing bytes. false_completions_observed was 0 across all seven classes.
falsifiable_hypothesis: A partial write, a pre-commit failure and a post-commit failure each leave a recoverable state and never a false completion.
limitations: SIGKILL skips the finally block that removes the temporary file, so each crashed write left a stray dotted entry (for example .000004-checkpointed.json.dlcc87xf). No custody assertion failed because the mechanism enumerates state by *.json glob and explicit filename, but the residue is never reclaimed.

The post-commit class satisfies this unit's hypothesis (recoverable state, no false completion) only because the bytes survive; automatic replay of that commit does not happen and is recorded separately as DEF-PO03-C6-042-LOST-CALLBACK-NOT-REPLAYED.

Crash points are reached by replacing os.link, os.open and os.replace inside the loaded module instance in the child process; this reproduces the instruction boundary faithfully but is not a power-loss test of the underlying filesystem.
provider_run_id is NOT_SUPPORTED because this runtime exposes no subagent spawn tool and therefore no separate provider run identifier.
